A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 7 - it would give a fat mass of only $0.005 \text{ kg}$ in $4.00 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^{3}$, not the $0.0366 \text{ kg}$ remaining after the fat-free milk is subtracted.

C.explanation: Slightly too large - close to the correct value but does not follow from $m_{fat} = 0.0366 \text{ kg}$ divided by $4.00 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^{3}$ with the given $1.040 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: Greater than the fat-free density $1.040 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, which cannot be correct because adding fat lowers the overall density from $1040$ to $1035 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.

hints: Notice the wording 4.00% fat by volume - split the total $1.000 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^{3}$ into a fat volume of $0.0400 \times 1.000 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^{3}$ and a fat-free volume of $0.960 \times 1.000 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^{3}$.
Connect total mass to component masses with $m = \rho V$ - the $1.035 \text{ kg}$ equals the mass of the fat-free part plus the mass of the fat part.
First calculate the fat-free mass using $1.040 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, subtract it from $1.035 \text{ kg}$ to leave the fat mass, then divide by the fat volume.
walkthrough: Find the two volumes from 4.00% by volume. $V_{fat} = 0.0400 \times 1.000 \times 10^{-3} = 4.00 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^{3}$ and $V_{free} = 0.960 \times 1.000 \times 10^{-3} = 9.60 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{3}$.
Use $m = \rho V$ for the fat-free milk of density $1.040 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$. $m_{free} = 1.040 \times 10^{3} \times 9.60 \times 10^{-4} = 0.9984 \text{ kg}$.
Apply mass conservation for the mixture. $m_{total} = m_{free} + m_{fat}$, so $m_{fat} = 1.035 - 0.9984 = 0.0366 \text{ kg}$.
Calculate the fat density with $\rho = m/V$. $\rho_{fat} = 0.0366 / 4.00 \times 10^{-5} = 915 \text{ kg m}^{-3} = 9.15 \times 10^{2} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Check sense: this is less than $1.040 \times 10^{3} \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, as required because the $1.035 \text{ kg}$ mixture is less dense than fat-free milk. This is option B.
